HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P) NOTE

History:
• Chief complaint: Constant lower-abdominal pain, midline, below the umbilicus.  
• Onset/duration: Began “a few days ago”; progressively worsening.  
• Severity: ~8/10.  
• Character/course: Present all the time; episodes of marked worsening.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Light pink vaginal bleeding since after last normal period (LMP ≈ 2–3 weeks ago).  
  – Nausea without vomiting.  
  – Constipation for one week last week; bowel movements now normal.  
  – Mild nonspecific vaginal discharge; denies foul odor.  
• Denies fever, rigors, shoulder pain, shortness of breath, dizziness/syncope, dysuria, urinary frequency/urgency, hematuria, weight loss, or rectal bleeding.  
• Menstrual/gynecologic: Irregular menses on contraceptive implant (in situ × 1 year). Last normal period 2–3 weeks ago. Last intercourse 4 days ago, sexually active.  
• Obstetric: G0. Home pregnancy test negative ≈ 1 month ago (none since symptom onset).  
• Triggers/relief: No specific triggers; pain affects daily activities but patient continues to work.

Past Medical History:
• Drug allergy: Amoxicillin – “allergy” (exact reaction not specified).  
• No chronic illnesses reported.  
• No prior surgeries or hospitalizations.  
• Medications: Etonogestrel contraceptive implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented. No other regular medications mentioned.

Physical Examination:
(Tele-consultation – no in-person exam performed.)  
• General: Patient alert, conversational, able to carry on normal activities.  
• No vital signs available.  
• No physical findings documented.

Impression:
Lower abdominal pain with light post-menstrual vaginal bleeding; rule out early pregnancy/ectopic pregnancy versus gynecologic or gastrointestinal causes.

Management Plan:
• Arrange urgent face-to-face clinic appointment for full abdominal and pelvic examination.  
• Advise patient to perform a urinary pregnancy test today; instructed to call immediately if positive.  
• Safety-netting: If pain worsens, develops vomiting preventing oral intake, or any new concerning symptoms, seek medical attention sooner (support line or emergency services).  
• No medications initiated during call.  
• Support line number provided for scheduling and urgent contact.

Patient Summary:
23-year-old woman with 3-day history of worsening constant midline lower-abdominal pain and light vaginal bleeding. On etonogestrel implant, last period 2–3 weeks ago, pregnancy test one month ago negative. Needs in-person evaluation and repeat pregnancy test to exclude ectopic pregnancy or other intra-abdominal pathology.

Key Takeaways:
• Do a urinary pregnancy test today and phone immediately if positive.  
• Call support line now to arrange same-day/next-day clinic examination.  
• Seek urgent care if pain acutely worsens or you cannot keep fluids down.

Next Steps:
• Urgent clinic visit for abdominal & pelvic exam and possible investigations (e.g., pelvic ultrasound, labs) after pregnancy status clarified.  
• Follow-up determined after face-to-face assessment.
